# 1 Samuel Chapter 26 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 165v-166r | **Source Image:** 1SA_026_page_001.jpg, 1SA_026_page_002.jpg

---

**26:1** And-came the-Zifim (Ziphites) to Sha'ul (Saul) to-the-Giv'ah (Gibeah), saying, "Is-not David hiding-himself in-[the]-hill of-the-Khakhilah (Hachilah), which [is] upon [the]-face of-the-Yeshimon (wasteland)?"

**26:2** And-arose Sha'ul (Saul), and-he-went-down to [the]-wilderness of-Zif (Ziph), and-with-him three thousand man, [the]-chosen-ones of-Yisra'el (Israel), to-seek David in-[the]-wilderness of-Zif (Ziph).

**26:3** And-encamped Sha'ul (Saul) in-[the]-hill of-the-Khakhilah (Hachilah), which [is] upon [the]-face of-the-Yeshimon (wasteland), upon the-way. And-David [was]-dwelling in-the-wilderness, and-he-saw that Sha'ul (Saul) came after-him to-the-wilderness.

**26:4** And-sent David spies, and-he-knew that Sha'ul (Saul) had-come to [a]-certainty.

**26:5** And-arose David, and-he-came to the-place where Sha'ul (Saul) had-encamped there, and-saw David the-place where lay Sha'ul (Saul), and-Avner (Abner) son of-Ner, [the]-commander of-his-army. And-Sha'ul (Saul) [was]-lying in-the-ma'gal (encampment), and-the-people [were]-encamping around-him.

**26:6** And-answered David and-he-said to Akhimelekh (Ahimelech) the-Khitti (Hittite), and-to Avishai (Abishai) son of-Tzeruyah (Zeruiah), brother of-Yo'av (Joab), saying, "Who will-go-down with-me to Sha'ul (Saul), to the-camp?" And-said Avishai (Abishai), "I will-go-down with-you."

**26:7** And-came David and-Avishai (Abishai) to the-people [by]-night, and-behold, Sha'ul (Saul) [was]-lying, sleeping, in-the-ma'gal (encampment), and-his-spear [was]-thrust in-the-ground at-his-head. And-Avner (Abner) and-the-people [were]-lying around-him.

**26:8** And-said Avishai (Abishai) to David, "Has-delivered-up God today your-enemy in-your-hand. And-now, let-me-strike-him, please, with-the-spear, and-into-the-ground one-stroke, and-I-will-not-repeat to-him."

**26:9** And-said David to Avishai (Abishai), "Do-not-destroy him, for who has-stretched-out his-hand against [the]-anointed-one of-YHWH and-been-innocent?"

**26:10** And-said David, "[As]-lives YHWH, surely YHWH will-strike-him, or his-day will-come and-he-will-die, or into-battle he-will-go-down and-he-will-be-swept-away.

**26:11** Far-be-it from-me, by-YHWH, from-stretching-out my-hand against [the]-anointed-one of-YHWH. And-now, take, please, the-spear which [is] at-his-head, and-the-jug of-water, and-let-us-go for-ourselves."

**26:12** And-took David the-spear and-the-jug of-water from-at [the]-head of-Sha'ul (Saul), and-they-went for-themselves, and-no-one [was]-seeing, and-no-one [was]-knowing, and-no-one [was]-awakening, for all-of-them [were]-sleeping, for a-deep-sleep of-YHWH had-fallen upon-them.

**26:13** And-crossed-over David to-the-other-side, and-he-stood upon [the]-top of-the-mountain from-afar -- great [was] the-place between-them.

**26:14** And-called-out David to the-people and-to Avner (Abner) son of-Ner, saying, "Will-you-not-answer, Avner (Abner)?" And-answered Avner (Abner) and-he-said, "Who [are] you [who]-call to the-king?"

**26:15** And-said David to Avner (Abner), "Are-not you a-man? And-who [is] like-you in-Yisra'el (Israel)? And-why have-you-not-guarded over your-lord the-king? For came one of-the-people to-destroy the-king your-lord.

**26:16** Not good [is] this thing which you-have-done. [As]-lives YHWH, surely sons of-death [are] you, because you-did-not-guard over your-lord, over [the]-anointed-one of-YHWH. And-now, see -- where [is] the-spear of-the-king and-the-jug of-water which [was] at his-head?"

**26:17** And-recognized Sha'ul (Saul) [the]-voice of-David, and-he-said, "Is-this your-voice, my-son David?" And-said David, "[It is] my-voice, my-lord the-king."

**26:18** And-he-said, "Why [is] this [that] my-lord pursues after his-servant? For what have-I-done, and-what [is the]-evil in-my-hand?

**26:19** And-now, let-hear, please, my-lord the-king the-words of-his-servant. If YHWH has-incited you against-me, let-Him-smell an-offering. And-if [the]-sons of-adam [have done so], cursed [are] they before YHWH, for they-have-driven-me-out today from-being-attached to-[the]-inheritance of-YHWH, saying, 'Go, serve gods of-other-[peoples].'

**26:20** And-now, let-not-fall my-blood to-the-ground away-from [the]-face of-YHWH, for has-gone-out the-king of-Yisra'el (Israel) to-seek a-single flea, as-one-pursues the-partridge in-the-mountains."

**26:21** And-said Sha'ul (Saul), "I-have-sinned. Return, my-son David, for I-will-not-do-evil to-you again, because that my-life [was]-precious in-your-eyes this day. Behold, I-have-been-foolish, and-I-have-erred exceedingly greatly."

**26:22** And-answered David and-he-said, "Behold, the-spear of-the-king. And-let-cross-over one of-the-young-men and-let-him-take it.

**26:23** And-YHWH will-return to-each-man his-righteousness and-his-faithfulness, [in]-that YHWH gave you today into-[my]-hand and-I-was-not-willing to-stretch-out my-hand against [the]-anointed-one of-YHWH.

**26:24** And-behold, as-was-great your-life in-my-eyes this day, so may-be-great my-life in-[the]-eyes of-YHWH, and-may-He-deliver-me from-all distress."

**26:25** And-said Sha'ul (Saul) to David, "Blessed [are] you, my-son David. Both doing you-will-do, and-also prevailing you-will-prevail." And-went David to-his-way, and-Sha'ul (Saul) returned to-his-place.

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **26:1** -- The Ziphites betray David a second time (cf. 23:19). The Leningrad Codex reads הֲלוֹא with the interrogative he, consistent with their earlier report.
2. **26:5** -- אַבְנֵר בֶּן־נֵר (Avner son of-Ner): The Leningrad text consistently uses the plene spelling. Avner serves as Sha'ul's chief military officer (שַׂר צְבָאוֹ). The term מַעְגָּל (ma'gal) denotes a circular wagon-camp or encampment formed by the baggage train.
3. **26:6** -- אֲחִימֶלֶךְ הַחִתִּי (Akhimelekh the Hittite): Not to be confused with Akhimelekh the priest (22:9-20). The presence of a Hittite in David's band indicates the cosmopolitan nature of his followers.
4. **26:8** -- הִסְגִּיר (has-delivered-up): The Hif'il of סגר conveys the sense of God closing/shutting the enemy into David's power.
5. **26:10** -- Three possible fates for Sha'ul are enumerated: divine striking (יִגְּפֶנּוּ), natural death (יוֹמוֹ יָבוֹא), or death in battle (יֵרֵד בַמִּלְחָמָה). The Leningrad vocalization of וְנִסְפָּה (and-he-will-be-swept-away) is Nif'al of ספה.
6. **26:12** -- תַּרְדֵּמַת יְהוָה (a-deep-sleep of-YHWH): The same word תַּרְדֵּמָה used of the deep sleep upon Adam (Gen 2:21) and Avram (Gen 15:12). Here it is directly attributed to YHWH.
7. **26:19** -- יָרִיחַ (let-Him-smell): From רוח in Hif'il, the idea of YHWH accepting a sacrifice by smelling its aroma (cf. Gen 8:21). The phrase "go serve other gods" (לֵךְ עֲבֹד אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים) reflects the ancient understanding that exile from the land meant exile from YHWH's domain.
8. **26:20** -- פַּרְעֹשׁ אֶחָד (a-single flea): Same self-deprecating comparison David used in 24:15 [Eng. 24:14]. The קֹרֵא (partridge, lit. "caller") is hunted in mountainous terrain.
9. **26:25** -- Sha'ul's final words to David in the book: גַּם עָשֹׂה תַעֲשֶׂה וְגַם יָכֹל תּוּכָל -- the doubled infinitive absolutes (doing you-will-do, prevailing you-will-prevail) express Sha'ul's resigned acknowledgment of David's inevitable triumph.

-- EMET
